# new-app

{{ONE_LINE_PROJECT_DESCRIPTION}}

## Stack

- Monorepo: pnpm workspaces (JS/TS) + uv workspace (Python), one repo
- Node ≥24, pnpm 12 (pinned via `packageManager`); Python 3.14 (`.python-version`), uv
- Frontend: Next.js 16 App Router in `apps/web` (TypeScript strict, Tailwind 4, React Compiler)
- UI: shadcn/ui preset `b4XwA3eDL6` (radix, vega, violet), Hugeicons. Internal dev-only reference: the /design page (404 in production); new UI must reuse it
- JS/TS lint + format: Biome (root `biome.json`). Python: ruff (lint + format), mypy strict, pytest
- Backend, database, auth, hosting: {{TBD}}. Choose per task and record the decision in docs/adr/

## Commands

| Task | Command |
| --- | --- |
| First setup | `pnpm setup` (pnpm install + uv sync --all-packages) |
| Dev server (web) | `pnpm dev` |
| Python sidecar | `pnpm dev:py` (FastAPI on :8000, docs at /docs) · both via Vercel: `pnpm dev:all` |
| Lint / format | `pnpm lint` · `pnpm format` |
| Type-check | `pnpm typecheck` (next typegen + tsc, mypy) |
| Test | `pnpm test` (JS packages + pytest) |
| Everything | `pnpm check` (lint → typecheck → test) |
| Build | `pnpm build` |
| One JS package | `pnpm --filter <name> <script>` |
| One Python member | `uv run --package <name> <cmd>` |
| Add a JS dependency | `pnpm --filter <name> add <dep>` (ask first) |
| Add a Python dependency | `uv add --package <name> <dep>` (ask first) |

Before calling a task done: `pnpm check` must pass.

## Architecture

- `apps/*`: deployable JS apps (pnpm). `apps/web` is the Next.js frontend; it has its own AGENTS.md with Next.js 16 guidance
- `packages/*`: shared JS/TS packages named `@new-app/<name>`, consumed with `workspace:*`
- `python/*`: uv workspace members (src layout, tests beside src). Cross-member deps use `{ workspace = true }`
- Next.js is the full-stack app. `python/api` is a PRIVATE FastAPI sidecar only for Python-only libraries
- Next server code calls Python via `apps/web/src/lib/python-api.ts`; `vercel.json` services bind it as `BACKEND_INTERNAL_URL`
- Root holds shared tooling only: `package.json` scripts, `pnpm-workspace.yaml`, `pyproject.toml` (ruff/mypy/pytest), `biome.json`
- Design context: PRODUCT.md (product truth, via Impeccable) and `apps/web/DESIGN.md` (visual system, a generated mirror of `globals.css`)
- Copy context: `VOICE.md` (voice, tone, vocabulary, claims policy). All user-facing words follow it; `pnpm copy:check` enforces it
- Design values only from tokens; no hardcoded colors, sizes, or fonts. `pnpm design:tokens` enforces it
- UI work runs Impeccable automatically (shape → harden/polish → audit); a hook gates turns that change UI
- Deep dives live in `docs/knowledge/`. See its README index; load only what the task needs.

## Conventions

- Read existing code before writing; follow nearby patterns, naming, and structure.
- Reuse first: search for existing utilities, components, and types before writing new ones.
- Prefer libraries already in the project; ask before adding a dependency.
- Verify library APIs against current docs, not memory.
- Single source of truth for constants, types, and config. No magic strings.
- Small, focused modules placed where project conventions say.
- Comment *why*, not *what*; match the surrounding comment density.

## Workflow

- Non-trivial work: plan first, then implement in small verifiable steps.
- One branch per change: `<feat|fix|chore|docs|refactor>/<short-slug>` off `main`. Conventional Commits.
- Never commit secrets, `.env*`, or build output. Never force-push shared branches.
- Get an independent review before merging.

## Do not

- Edit generated files: `apps/web/DESIGN.md`, `apps/web/next-env.d.ts`, `pnpm-lock.yaml`, `uv.lock`, `GEMINI.md`, `context-pack*.md`, `.github/copilot-instructions.md`, `.cursor/rules/`.
- Touch `vercel.json`, `.github/workflows/`, `.env*`, `components.json` without asking.
- Disable lint rules, type checks, or tests to make something pass.
- Run destructive commands (DB drops, `rm -rf`, `git reset --hard`, force push) without explicit confirmation.

## Environment

- Required env var names are in `apps/web/.env.example` and `python/api/.env.example`. Never read or print secret values.
- Local services: none yet (Next on :3000, Python sidecar on :8000)

## Knowledge upkeep

- Record new lessons in `.claude/inbox.md` (one line each); never append to this file directly.
- This file has a hard budget. When it's full, demote detail to `docs/knowledge/` and leave a one-line pointer.

## Always-on rules

# Code style

- Match the style of the file you are editing before applying any rule below.
- TS: camelCase vars/functions, PascalCase types and components, SCREAMING_SNAKE constants. Python: PEP 8 naming (ruff `N`).
- TS exports: named exports, except where Next.js requires default (`page`, `layout`, `route` files).
- Imports: alias `@/*` in apps; workspace packages as `@new-app/<name>`; Biome and ruff own import order.
- Functions: small, single-purpose; early returns over nested conditionals.
- Types: TS strict with no `any`; Python fully typed for mypy strict. Explicit types at module boundaries.
- Errors: never swallow them; handle at boundaries with typed errors.
- Constants and config live in one module per package. No magic numbers or strings inline.
- Comments explain *why*. Delete commented-out code.
- Formatting is owned by Biome (JS/TS) and ruff (Python); the PostToolUse hook runs them.

# Context hygiene

- New lessons go to `.claude/inbox.md` via `/learn`; never append to AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, or rules directly.
- One fact per bullet, imperative, ≤30 words. No stories or dates in hot files.
- Don't write what the code already says (commands, structure); it is injected at session start.
- Never edit generated files (GEMINI.md, `context-pack*.md`, `.github/copilot-instructions.md`, `.cursor/rules/`); edit the source.
- When the context linter reports a violation, fix it before continuing.

# Git

- Branch names: `<feat|fix|chore|docs|refactor>/<short-slug>`. Never commit straight to `main`.
- Commits: Conventional Commits, imperative subject ≤ 72 chars, body explains *why*.
- One logical change per commit. Don't mix refactors with behavior changes.
- Before committing: lint, type-check, and the relevant tests pass.
- Never: force-push shared branches, rewrite published history, commit `.env*` or build output.
- PRs: use `/review` first; the description covers what, why, how it was tested, and screenshots for UI.

# Security

- Never read, print, log, or commit secrets. Use env vars; reference `apps/web/.env.example` / `python/api/.env.example` for names only.
- Validate and parse all external input at the boundary (Zod in TS, Pydantic in Python).
- Parameterized queries only. No string-built SQL, shell, or HTML.
- AuthN/AuthZ checks go on the server, on every protected route/action. Never trust the client.
- Escape output by default. No `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` / `eval` / `exec` with user data.
- New dependency → check maintenance, license, and known CVEs; ask before adding.
- Least privilege for tokens, DB roles, and cloud IAM.
- When in doubt, stop and flag it to the user instead of guessing.

## Path-specific rules

_Applies to `src/app/api/**, **/server/**, **/routes/**, **/actions/**`_

# API / server

- Validate request input with {{VALIDATION_LIB}} schemas at the edge of every handler.
- Response shape: {{e.g. `{ data: T } | { error: { code, message } }`}}; consistent HTTP status codes.
- AuthZ check first, before any data access.
- Business logic lives in {{SERVICE_LAYER_PATH}}; handlers stay thin.
- Idempotency for retries on mutating endpoints where clients may retry.
- Log with structured fields; never log secrets or PII.
- Rate-limit public endpoints. Paginate list endpoints.

_Applies to `**/migrations/**, **/schema.*, **/*.sql, {prisma,drizzle,convex,db}/**`_

# Database

- Schema changes go through migrations ({{MIGRATION_TOOL}}). Never edit applied migrations.
- Migrations must be backward compatible with the currently deployed code (expand → migrate → contract).
- Every foreign key and frequent filter column gets an index. Justify any missing one.
- No destructive migration (drop/rename column/table) without explicit user approval.
- Seed data lives in {{SEED_PATH}}. Never point local tooling at production.

_Applies to `docs/**, **/*.md, **/*.mdx`_

# Documentation

- Audience first: say who the doc is for in its first paragraph.
- Keep README for setup and usage; architecture lives in docs/architecture.md; decisions in docs/adr/NNNN-title.md.
- Commands in docs must be copy-pasteable and tested.
- Update docs in the same change as the behavior they describe.

_Applies to `apps/web/**, packages/**/*.{ts,tsx}`_

# Frontend (Next.js 16, apps/web)

- Read `apps/web/node_modules/next/dist/docs/` for the relevant guide before writing Next.js code. APIs changed since training data.
- App Router only: routes in `src/app/`, Server Components by default, add `"use client"` only for interactivity or browser APIs.
- Keep route files (`page.tsx`, `layout.tsx`, `route.ts`) thin; put logic in `src/lib/` or `src/features/<feature>/`.
- UI components go in `src/components/` (PascalCase files). Shared cross-app code goes in `packages/*` as `@new-app/<name>`.
- Import with the `@/*` alias, never deep relative paths across features.
- React Compiler is on: don't hand-write `useMemo`/`useCallback`/`memo` for performance.
- Design system: follow the `design-system` skill. Reuse the compositions on the /design page (`src/app/design/_preview/`) and the shadcn components in `src/components/ui/`.
- Add components from `apps/web`: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add <name>`. Animated libraries: see design-system `libraries.md` (free only, never `--overwrite`).
- Class merging: `cn` from `@/lib/utils`. Icons: Hugeicons (`@hugeicons/react`), per `components.json`.
- Design values come ONLY from tokens: semantic colors (`bg-primary`, `text-muted-foreground`), the Tailwind spacing and type scales, `rounded-*`, and `font-heading` / `font-sans`.
- Never hardcode: no hex/rgb/oklch literals, palette classes (`zinc-500`), arbitrary values (`w-[123px]`), or inline style literals. A hook blocks them.
- Need a new value? Add a token in `globals.css`; `DESIGN.md` regenerates to mirror it (`pnpm design:sync`). Never edit `DESIGN.md` tokens.
- Use `next/image`, `next/font`, and `next/link`; never raw `<img>` or `<a>` for internal routes.
- Route types (`PageProps`, `LayoutProps`) are generated by `next typegen`; don't redeclare them.
- Accessibility: semantic HTML, labelled controls, keyboard reachable, visible focus.
- Lint and format with Biome only (`pnpm lint:js`, `pnpm format`); no ESLint or Prettier.

_Applies to `python/**, **/*.py, pyproject.toml`_

# Python (uv workspace)

- Manage everything with uv: `uv add --package <member> <dep>`, `uv run ...`. Never pip, venv, or poetry.
- New member: `uv init --lib python/<name>` (library) or `--app` (service). Name it `new-app-<name>`, import as `new_app_<name>`.
- src layout: code in `python/<name>/src/new_app_<name>/`, tests in `python/<name>/tests/test_*.py`.
- Cross-member dependency: `uv add --package <consumer> new-app-<member>`; uv writes `{ workspace = true }`.
- Shared tooling config lives only in the root `pyproject.toml` (ruff, mypy, pytest). Don't add per-member copies.
- Full type hints; `mypy --strict` must pass. Use `py.typed` in libraries.
- ruff owns lint and format (`pnpm lint:py`, `pnpm format`). Fix the warnings instead of adding `noqa`.
- `python/api` is a private sidecar: add endpoints only for Python-only needs; everything else belongs in Next.js.
- New endpoint: Pydantic models in `models.py`, a test in `tests/`, and the matching typed function in `apps/web/src/lib/python-api.ts`.
- Commit `uv.lock`; never edit it by hand.

_Applies to `**/*.test.*, **/*.spec.*, **/__tests__/**, **/tests/**, e2e/**`_

# Testing

- Python: pytest, files `python/<member>/tests/test_*.py`. Run one with `uv run pytest <path>`.
- JS/TS: no runner chosen yet. Ask before adding one, and wire it as a `test` script so `pnpm test` picks it up.
- Names: "should <expected> when <condition>" (JS) / `test_<behavior>_when_<condition>` (Python).
- Arrange / Act / Assert. One behavior per test.
- Mock at the boundaries (network, time, randomness, FS). Don't mock the unit under test.
- Bug fix → write a failing test first, then fix.
- No `.only` / `.skip` committed. No sleeps; use fake timers or await conditions.
